QF.id: AIFM Fund Monitoring, Reporting, and Exit_25

question.text: Mr. Dhruv Menon, IR head at Sindhu Opportunities Fund, is designing the standard quarterly LP report. Which of the following sets of line-items BEST matches ILPA-style contents that Indian Cat II AIFs typically include?

answer.text: Trustee meeting minutes, IC decisions, GP travel expenses, director remuneration
Clearing-member margin usage, VaR, derivative exposure, daily P&L
SEBI activity return, KRA/CKYC status, AML red flags, STR filings
NAV, DPI/RVPI/TVPI multiples, realised and unrealised gains, capital-account activity, portfolio snapshot, material events

explanation.text: The Logic: ILPA-aligned quarterly LP reports for closed-ended private-market funds focus on: NAV, performance multiples (DPI = distributions / paid-in, RVPI = residual value / paid-in, TVPI = total / paid-in), realised/unrealised gains, capital-call / distribution activity, portfolio snapshot, and material events. Cat III (listed-derivative heavy) funds additionally report leverage per SEBI. The Trap: Option B suits a trading desk / Cat III hedge fund, not a Cat II quarterly. Option C is regulatory/AML operational content, not LP reporting. Option D is internal-governance material rarely surfaced to all LPs. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A/B touch NAV reporting only. XIX-C expects the multiples vocabulary (DPI/RVPI/TVPI) that an LP investor in a Cat II fund will quiz you on. Manager's Pro-Tip: Publish DPI/RVPI/TVPI EVERY quarter — even if TVPI barely moves. LPs benchmark against Preqin/Pitchbook peer vintages, and consistent disclosure builds the trust you need when you raise Fund II.
